newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public sector unions call Oct 17 strike.
newsitem.headline: French public sector unions call Oct 17 strike.

text.p: France's largest public sector unions on Monday urged some four million state workers to strike for 24 hours on October 17 to press for wage increases and protest against government plans to reduce state payrolls.

"This is an appeal for a 24-hour strike. We are going to do all we can to make sure it succeeds," Philippe Antoine, deputy director of the federation of civil service workers at the giant CFDT union, told Reuters.
Union officials said the appeal for a "national day of action, strikes and protests" would hit all public sector functions including hospitals, state agencies, and local governments.
About one in five employees in France work in the civil service at the national or local level. Unions say that workers are taking the brunt of the centre-right government's austerity policies.

Yet despite union warnings that discontent is boiling up, most analysts believe prospects are remote of strikes on the scale of the crippling stoppages that paralysed much of France last November and December.
The seven main civil service unions had decided on September 10 to appeal for a one-day strike. Monday's meeting of union officials was to fix the date.
The principal unions in France's civil service are seeking the immediate opening of wage talks with the government despite Prime Minister Alain Juppe's freeze on wage increases this year.
Juppe's budget plans for next year including trimming civil service numbers by about 6,000 workers, many of them national teaching posts.
Though this would be accomplished primarily by erosion rather than lay-offs, unions fear this is only a start.
Unions are also upset by state spending cuts proposed for next year which would bring public deficits to less than three percent of France's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
The cuts are intended to help France qualify for European monetary union from 1999.
